author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Base rule matching a single failed interactive or network logon. It is not intended to alert on its own; the correlation rule below applies the threshold.
false_positives: Expired passwords and stale saved credentials on service accounts.
name: Failed Windows Logon

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects sudo being used to launch an interactive shell or a language interpreter. Both give an unrestricted root session, which defeats the point of granting narrow sudo rules, and is the usual outcome of exploiting a permissive sudoers entry.
false_positives: Administrators who legitimately hold full sudo rights. The rule is most useful where sudo is scoped to specific commands.
name: Sudo Invocation of a Shell or Interpreter

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects a cron entry being created that invokes a network client or an interpreter. Package managers install cron jobs too, so the payload rather than the write is what makes this interesting.
false_positives: Configuration management such as Ansible or Puppet writing cron entries. Filter on the parent process of the automation agent.
name: Cron Persistence Written Outside Package Management
query: ((process.command_line : "*crontab -*" or process.command_line : "*/etc/cron.d/*" or process.command_line : "*/var/spool/cron/*") and (process.command_line : "*curl*" or process.command_line : "*wget*" or process.command_line : "*/dev/tcp/*" or process.command_line : "*base64*" or process.command_line : "*python*" or process.command_line : "*perl*" or process.command_line : "*bash -i*") and not (process.parent.name : "dpkg" or process.parent.name : "apt" or process.parent.name : "rpm" or process.parent.name : "yum" or process.parent.name : "dnf"))

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects curl or wget output piped straight into a shell. Nothing is written to disk for a scanner to inspect, and the fetched content is executed with the caller's privileges, so this is a common first-stage installer for Linux implants and cryptominers.
false_positives: Documented installation instructions for developer tooling use this pattern. On a server outside a build pipeline it should be rare enough to alert on.
name: Remote Script Downloaded and Piped Directly to a Shell
note: Investigation fields: process.command_line, process.parent.name, user.name, host.name

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects the recognisable one-liners that redirect a shell over a network socket, covering the bash /dev/tcp form, netcat with an execution flag, and the Python socket-to-pty pattern.
false_positives: Authorised penetration tests and red-team exercises. Correlate with the engagement window.
name: Interactive Reverse Shell Invocation
note: Investigation fields: process.command_line, process.parent.name, destination.ip, destination.port, user.name
query: ((process.command_line:*\/dev\/tcp\/* OR process.command_line:*\/dev\/udp\/*) OR process.command_line:/.*\bn(c|cat|etcat)\b.*\s-[a-zA-Z]*e\b.*/ OR ((process.command_line:*socket* AND process.command_line:*subprocess*) AND (process.command_line:*pty.spawn* OR process.command_line:*dup2*)))

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects rundll32 or regsvr32 executing content from a remote location or from a user-writable path. Both are Microsoft-signed and allowed by most application control policies, which is exactly why they are used to run attacker code.
false_positives: Some enterprise software registers COM objects from ProgramData during install. Scope by parent process where that occurs.
name: Signed Binary Proxy Execution via rundll32 or regsvr32
query: ((process.name : "rundll32.exe" or process.name : "regsvr32.exe") and ((process.command_line : "*http://*" or process.command_line : "*https://*" or process.command_line : "*\\\\\\\\*" or process.command_line : "*scrobj.dll*" or process.command_line : "*{'javascript': None}*" or process.command_line : "*{'vbscript': None}*") or (process.command_line : "*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" or process.command_line : "*\\Users\\Public\\*" or process.command_line : "*\\Downloads\\*")))

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects processes reading LSASS memory or command lines that name LSASS alongside a dumping utility. LSASS holds cached credential material, so a memory dump of it is a direct precursor to lateral movement.
false_positives: Endpoint protection products and crash-reporting agents legitimately open LSASS. Baseline the accessing image path before enabling this rule in production.
name: Credential Dumping Indicators Against LSASS
note: Investigation fields: process.name, process.executable, process.command_line, process.target.name, user.name
query: ((((winlog.event_id : "10" and process.target.name : "*\\lsass.exe") and (process.access_mask : "*0x1010*" or process.access_mask : "*0x1410*" or process.access_mask : "*0x143a*")) or (process.command_line : "*lsass*" and (process.command_line : "*procdump*" or process.command_line : "*comsvcs.dll*" or process.command_line : "*MiniDump*" or process.command_line : "*rundll32*"))) and not (process.executable : "C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender\\*" or process.executable : "C:\\Windows\\System32\\wbem\\*"))

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects a Microsoft Office process creating a command shell or script host. Office has no legitimate reason to start these in most environments, and this parent-child pair is the usual first observable step of a macro-enabled phishing document.
false_positives: Line-of-business Office add-ins and document templates that shell out. These are rare and worth enumerating once rather than suppressing the rule.
name: Office Application Spawning a Script Interpreter
note: Investigation fields: process.parent.name, process.name, process.command_line, user.name
query: ((process.parent.name : "winword.exe" or process.parent.name : "excel.exe" or process.parent.name : "powerpnt.exe" or process.parent.name : "outlook.exe" or process.parent.name : "msaccess.exe") and (process.name : "cmd.exe" or process.name : "powershell.exe" or process.name : "pwsh.exe" or process.name : "wscript.exe" or process.name : "cscript.exe" or process.name : "mshta.exe" or process.name : "regsvr32.exe" or process.name : "rundll32.exe"))

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects a PowerShell command line that both retrieves remote content and executes it in memory. The pairing matters: a download alone is ordinary, and Invoke-Expression alone is ordinary, but together they are the standard shape of a staged payload that never touches disk.
false_positives: Package bootstrap scripts such as the Chocolatey installer follow exactly this pattern. Allow-list by the specific URL host rather than by the technique.
name: PowerShell Download Cradle
query: ((process.name : "powershell.exe" or process.name : "pwsh.exe") and (process.command_line : "*DownloadString*" or process.command_line : "*DownloadFile*" or process.command_line : "*DownloadData*" or process.command_line : "*Invoke-WebRequest*" or process.command_line : "*Net.WebClient*" or process.command_line : "*iwr*" or process.command_line : "*curl*") and (process.command_line : "*IEX*" or process.command_line : "*Invoke-Expression*" or process.command_line : "*| iex*" or process.command_line : "*Start-Process*"))

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects powershell.exe invoked with an encoded command payload. Encoding is used to keep the real command out of the command line that defenders and logging see, and is common in loaders delivered by phishing documents.
false_positives: Configuration management and deployment tooling that wraps PowerShell payloads, notably SCCM and some backup agents. Baseline the parent process before alerting.
name: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution
note: Investigation fields: process.command_line, process.parent.name, user.name, host.name
query: ((process.name : "powershell.exe" or process.name : "pwsh.exe" or process.executable : "*\\powershell.exe") and (process.command_line : "* -enc *" or process.command_line : "* -encodedcommand*" or process.command_line : "* -e *" or process.command_line : "* -ec *"))

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects a value being written to a Run key where the payload points at a script interpreter or a binary in a user-writable directory. Writing to Run keys is normal for installed software; the combination with a scripting host or a temp path is not.
false_positives: Installers that place updater shims under ProgramData. Confirm the publisher of the target binary before escalating.
name: Autorun Registry Key Written With a Suspicious Payload
note: Investigation fields: registry.path, registry.data.strings, process.name, user.name
query: ((registry.path : "*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\*" or registry.path : "*\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\*" or registry.path : "*\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Shell Folders\\Startup*") and (registry.data.strings : "*powershell*" or registry.data.strings : "*wscript*" or registry.data.strings : "*cscript*" or registry.data.strings : "*mshta*" or registry.data.strings : "*rundll32*" or registry.data.strings : "*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" or registry.data.strings : "*\\Users\\Public\\*" or registry.data.strings : "*\\ProgramData\\*"))

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects schtasks.exe creating a task. Scheduled tasks are a common persistence mechanism because they survive reboot and run without an interactive session. The signal is weak on its own, so the rule records the parent process to support triage rather than to justify an alert by itself.
false_positives: Software installers routinely register update tasks. Expect a high base rate and triage on the task action rather than on the creation event alone.
name: Scheduled Task Created From a Command Shell

author: Kamil Mete Yalcinkaya
description: Detects Windows service installation events whose service name or image path matches remote execution utilities. PsExec and its reimplementations work by writing a service binary to ADMIN$ and registering it, so the service installation event is the durable artefact.
false_positives: Administrators who use PsExec as a sanctioned remote administration tool. Where that is the case, scope the rule to source hosts outside the administrative subnet.
name: Service Creation Consistent With Remote Execution Tooling
note: Investigation fields: service.name, file.path, user.name, host.name
query: (event.code : "7045" and ((service.name : "*PSEXESVC*" or service.name : "*PAExec*" or service.name : "*RemComSvc*" or service.name : "*CSExec*") or (file.path : "*\\PSEXESVC.exe*" or file.path : "*\\paexec*" or file.path : "*\\RemComSvc.exe*")))
